A.note: Readable wide shot with the rock, sea and ships. The camps are flat tan rectangles with tiny uniform dots. The grass is oversaturated and patchy. The sea is a flat blue colour field. There is no atmosphere and no sign of a siege.

B.note: A top-down view of tent-like white cubes laid out in a rigid grid on flat tan slabs, which reads as a board game. The trench line is the only interesting element. There is no horizon, no fortress and no context, so the shot is hard to read.

C.note: The same composition as A, but the colours are more natural. The grass is more textured, the vegetation is darker, and the sea has some cloud reflection and a softer horizon. The camps are still flat tan slabs and the shot is still sparse.

why: C has the most natural colour, vegetation and water, and the clearest sense of place. A is similar but garish, and B is a toy-like grid with no context.
top_fix_for_best: Replace the flat tan camp rectangles with textured trampled-earth ground. Add varied tents, fires, smoke, palisades and trenches, and figures in irregular clusters. Then add depth with atmospheric haze, a low sun with long shadows, and a foreground element, so the besieged rock reads as the focus.
